issues.description: PR title/changelog says 'compute_image_not_publicly_shared' but PR description still names 'compute_image_publicly_shared' — branding drift between artifacts.
issues.detail: The CHANGELOG entry, directory, file, and class are all 'compute_image_not_publicly_shared', but the PR description still refers to the check as 'compute_image_publicly_shared/'. A reader auditing the diff against the description will stumble. Pick one name and use it everywhere the reader will look.

issues.description: Silent failure on getIamPolicy is reported as publicly_shared=False — same label as a verified-private image.
issues.detail: In `_get_images()`, when `getIamPolicy` throws (e.g., 403 Permission denied as exercised by test-image-3), the code logs the error and falls through with `publicly_shared=False`. The check then emits PASS with text 'is not publicly shared.' That is asymptotically-wrong as a security claim: an image whose policy we could not read is being asserted to be safe. Either skip the image (don't append), or add a tri-state (`policy_unknown`) and emit MANUAL/ERROR rather than PASS. The current test for test-image-3 actually pins the wrong behavior in place.

issues.description: `Image.id` is typed `str` but the GCP `images().list` payload returns `id` as a numeric string that is only sometimes present — no `.get` defensive access.
issues.detail: The code does `image['id']` and `image['name']` with bracket indexing. If GCP omits `id` for any reason (deletion in flight, partial response), this raises KeyError inside the inner try, which is silently swallowed only for the IAM call — the outer try catches it but the entire project's image enumeration is aborted from that point. Use `image.get('id', '')` / `image.get('name')` and skip on missing name. State the invariant: 'every appended Image has a non-empty name; id may be empty string.'

issues.description: Loop invariant of the bindings scan is not stated; `break` on first match is correct but undocumented.
issues.detail: The inner loop scans `iam_policy.get('bindings', [])` and sets `publicly_shared = True` then breaks. The invariant ('publicly_shared is True iff some binding's members contains allAuthenticatedUsers') is obvious to a careful reader but worth a single literate-comment line, especially since the role attached to that binding is ignored — any role grant to allAuthenticatedUsers counts as public, which is the intended semantics but is not explicit. One line of comment makes the policy explicit and the next reviewer faster.

issues.description: Complexity / API-call cost is N images × 1 getIamPolicy call serially per project, no batching, no concurrency — and it runs outside the existing `__threading_call__` pattern.
issues.detail: Sibling enumerations in `__init__` use `self.__threading_call__(...)` to parallelize across regions/zones. `_get_images` is invoked once, serially, and inside it issues one synchronous getIamPolicy per image per project. For a project with M custom images across P projects, that is O(P*M) sequential round trips. The big-O is unavoidable per image, but the constants kill it; this is ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW. Consider parallelizing across `self.project_ids` the way the rest of the file does, or at minimum noting why this one stays serial.

issues.description: `images().list(project=...)` returns public Google-published images by default unless filtered; the check name and metadata claim 'custom images' only.
issues.detail: The metadata and class docstring both say 'custom disk images.' But `client.images().list(project=project_id)` lists images owned by that project — which is correct for custom images only if the caller's project_id is the owner. Worth a one-line comment stating the invariant ('listing images owned by project_id; public Google-curated images live in separate projects like debian-cloud and are not returned here') so the next reader doesn't add a redundant filter or doubt the scope.

issues.description: Test `test_compute_no_images` does not set `compute_client.project_ids`, so it is not a regression test for the loop; it tests the trivial empty-list path only.
issues.detail: The check iterates `compute_client.images` directly, not project_ids, so the test works — but as a literate-test it should still set project_ids for consistency with the others, and it does not assert that getIamPolicy was not called. Minor; flagging because a reader of the test file will wonder.

issues.description: Service-level test pins the silent-failure behavior on test-image-3 as `publicly_shared=False` — codifies the wrong-on-error semantic flagged above.
issues.detail: `compute_service_test.py` asserts `not compute_client.images[2].publicly_shared` for the image whose getIamPolicy raised. If you fix the silent-failure issue by introducing a tri-state or skipping the image, this assertion becomes the artifact that prevents the fix from landing cleanly. Test should be rewritten to assert the unknown/skip semantics directly.

review.summary: The check is structurally simple and the algorithm is correct for the happy path — iterate images, scan bindings for allAuthenticatedUsers, emit PASS/FAIL. UNDER-AUDITED on two counts: (1) the IAM-policy fetch silently degrades to `publicly_shared=False`, which is reported as PASS — a security check claiming 'not publicly shared' for an image whose policy was unreadable is the wrong default and is currently pinned by tests; (2) the loop invariant and the 'any role to allAuthenticatedUsers is public' policy are not stated in a literate comment. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the bindings scan and on the 'custom images' scoping (it works because we list per owned project, but say so). ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW: one serial getIamPolicy per image per project, while sibling enumerations parallelize via `__threading_call__`; not a blocker but constants will hurt large estates. Naming drift between PR description ('compute_image_publicly_shared') and the actual artifact ('compute_image_not_publicly_shared') should be reconciled before merge.
